trust_section_content: Home Nura is an independent guide dedicated to air fryers, launched in 2024 and published for Europe and North America. Our methodology rests on five transparent criteria: cooking quality, value for money, ease of use, energy consumption and design. Each shortlisted model is evaluated using manufacturer specifications, cross-checked verified user reviews (Amazon, Google) and tests published by the specialist press. The Nura Score /10 combines these criteria into a single weighted score. Our only source of revenue is the Amazon EU Partner Program, disclosed on every link: no manufacturer can buy a better score, and our rankings remain strictly independent.
market_section_title: The Air Fryer Market in 2026: A Look at France
market_section_content: France offers a clear snapshot of how fast the air fryer market is growing. In 2026, more than 35% of French households own at least one air fryer, up from 18% in 2022, and the sector brings in more than €480 million a year in France. The leading brands there are Philips (30% market share), Ninja (22%), Cosori (15%), Moulinex (12%), Tefal (10%) and others (11%). Prices in France run from the equivalent of about $80 for entry-level models to more than $1,000 for high-end premium models, but most French buyers stick to the $250 to $600 range, where the best quality is concentrated. Key trends include strong demand for smart models (38% of sales), XXL sizes for large families (42% annual growth) and dual-basket models (a 26% share). French kitchens, traditionally attached to classic cooking methods, are gradually turning to air fryers for their energy efficiency and versatility.

recommendation_section_title: Quick Guide: Which Air Fryer Is Right for You?
recommendation_section_content: Just starting out and want something budget-friendly? The Cosori Lite (2.6 L / 2.7 qt) and Tefal Compact (4 L / 4.2 qt) offer excellent entry-level value, with solid performance and intuitive controls that suit first-time buyers. Large household (5 or more people)? Go for an XXL model such as the Ninja AF500 (5.2 L / 5.5 qt) or the Philips 6L XL, which handle family meals with ease, and pick a dual-basket model if you need to cook two dishes at once. Tech-savvy and want app control? The Ninja Foodi Smart (Wi-Fi-enabled) and the Philips Connected range offer full control from your phone, smart presets and cooking history tracking. Want to use less energy and cut your bills? The Cosori Pro (1,500 W) and Tefal Precision (1,400 W) use 15 to 20% less power than average models while keeping top-tier heating performance. Sensitive to noise? The Philips Compact (under 70 dB) and Ninja Whisper Series run quietly, ideal for open-concept kitchens. On a tight budget (under $120)? The Cecotec Compact (2 L / 2.1 qt) and Costway Ultra (1.8 L / 1.9 qt) deliver solid frying performance without the premium price tag. Love to cook and want plenty of variety? The Philips Premium Series includes more than 200 recipes, and the Ninja Foodi offers 101 preset programs covering everything from appetizers to desserts.
guide_intro_title: How to choose the best air fryer in 2026
guide_intro_text: The air fryer market keeps growing quickly, and models from Ninja, Philips, Cosori and Tefal lead the field. Our in-depth comparison guide helps you find the right air fryer for your budget, household size and cooking habits.
guide_criteria_capacity: Capacity: 2–3 L (about 2–3 qt) for 1–2 people, 4–5 L (about 4–5 qt) for 3–4 people and 6 L (about 6 qt) or more for large families. Dual-basket models let you cook two dishes at the same time.
guide_criteria_power: Power: 1,000–2,200 W. Higher wattage means faster preheating, and models rated 1,400–1,800 W offer the best balance. Canadian outlets supply 120 V, and a standard 15 A circuit delivers up to 1,800 W.
guide_criteria_features: Features: automatic programs, Wi-Fi connectivity, timer and keep-warm. Smart models let you control the air fryer from your phone.

faq.question: How does an air fryer work?
faq.answer: An air fryer uses a powerful fan to circulate very hot air around food, creating a crispy finish similar to deep frying but with up to 80% less fat. Rapid Air technology spreads the heat evenly for consistent results every time.

faq.question: What size air fryer do I need for my family?
faq.answer: For 1 or 2 people, a 2 to 3 L (about 2 to 3 qt) model is enough. For a family of 3 or 4, go for 4 to 5 L (about 4 to 5 qt). For 5 or more people, choose an XXL model of 6 L (about 6 qt) or more. Dual-basket models let you cook two dishes at once, which is perfect for busy households.

faq.question: Do air fryers use a lot of electricity?
faq.answer: No, air fryers are very energy efficient. They typically draw 1,000 to 1,700 W and cook faster than a conventional oven, cutting energy use by 30 to 50%. With regular use over a year, you could save roughly $20 to $30 on your electricity bill compared with a traditional oven, at an example rate of 10¢ per kWh.

faq.question: Can you cook frozen food in an air fryer?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Air fryers are great with frozen foods: fries, nuggets, onion rings, breaded vegetables. There's no need to thaw them first. Cooking time is typically 20% shorter than in an oven, and the results are crispier.

faq.question: What is the difference between an air fryer and a convection oven?
faq.answer: An air fryer is essentially a compact, concentrated convection oven. Its smaller size allows more intense air circulation and near-instant preheating. The result: faster cooking, crispier food and lower energy use than a full-size oven.

faq.question: Which air fryer is best for a family of four?
faq.answer: For a family of four, we recommend an air fryer with a capacity of 4 to 6 litres (about 4 to 6 quarts). The Cosori Dual Blaze (6.4 L / 6.8 qt) offers outstanding value, with dual heating elements that deliver perfectly even browning. The Philips Airfryer 3000 XL (6.2 L / 6.6 qt) is another excellent choice thanks to its proven reliability and Rapid Air technology. For families who often cook large batches, the Ninja Foodi MAX Double Stack (9.5 L / 10 qt) lets you prepare two completely different dishes at the same time. Expect to spend $200 to $400 for a model that performs well and lasts.

faq.question: How much does a good air fryer cost in 2026?
faq.answer: In 2026, air fryer prices vary widely depending on features and capacity. As a rough guide, entry-level models run $100 to $150, mid-range models $200 to $300 and premium models $400 to $600. Entry-level picks such as the Cosori Lite and Tefal Compact suit beginners and small kitchens. The mid-range offers the best value, with models such as the Philips 3000 XL and Cosori Dual Blaze. Premium models such as the Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer and Philips Combi XXL Connected add Wi-Fi connectivity, extra-large capacities and advanced cooking functions. Our advice: a budget of $150 to $300 gets you a high-performing model that should last five years or more.

faq.question: How do you clean an air fryer properly?
faq.answer: Regular cleaning keeps your air fryer performing well and helps it last longer. After each use, let the appliance cool for 10 to 15 minutes. Remove the basket and drawer, then wash them in warm, soapy water or put them in the dishwasher (check your manual to see if they're dishwasher-safe). For stubborn residue, soak them in warm water with baking soda for 15 minutes. Wipe the inside of the unit with a damp cloth — never submerge the main body in water. To get rid of lingering odours, run the air fryer empty for 5 minutes with half a lemon in the basket. A thorough deep clean once a month can extend your appliance's lifespan by 2 to 3 years.

faq.question: How much electricity does an air fryer actually use?
faq.answer: An air fryer uses far less electricity than a traditional oven. A standard air fryer draws 800 to 1,800 W, averaging around 1,400 W for mid-range models. By comparison, a conventional oven uses 2,000 to 3,000 W. Based on manufacturers' rated power, an air fryer uses roughly 0.7 kWh to cook a full meal (fries and chicken for four), compared with 1.8 kWh for the same meal in an oven. With regular use (4 to 5 times a week), that adds up to about 230 to 290 kWh saved over a year, or roughly $23 to $29 at an example rate of 10¢ per kWh. Your actual rate depends on your province and utility, so check your bill. The most efficient models in our comparison are the Xiaomi Smart Air Fryer Pro (800 W) and the Cosori Lite (900 W) for smaller portions.

faq.question: Can you bake cakes and pastries in an air fryer?
faq.answer: Yes, air fryers are surprisingly versatile for baking. You can make muffins, brownies, cookies, small cakes and even bread. The trick is to lower the temperature by about 20°C (about 35°F) compared with standard oven recipes and keep a closer eye on the bake, since the circulating hot air speeds things up. Use silicone moulds or paper liners that fit your basket. Models with a flat base, such as the Philips Combi XXL, are best suited for baking. Common guidelines: brownies at 150°C (300°F) for 15 minutes, muffins at 160°C (325°F) for 12 minutes and cookies at 160°C (325°F) for 8 minutes. The result: soft and moist inside, crisp outside, with virtually no preheating time.

faq.question: Air fryer vs. deep fryer: what's the difference?
faq.answer: The fundamental difference is the cooking method. A traditional deep fryer submerges food in 2 to 3 litres of hot oil (around 175°C, or 350°F), while an air fryer rapidly circulates very hot air instead. In practice, fries from an air fryer are slightly less crispy than deep-fried ones but contain up to 80% less fat. Health-wise, air frying dramatically reduces acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound that forms during high-temperature frying. Air fryers are also safer to use (no risk of hot oil splattering), much easier to clean and far more versatile — you can roast, broil and reheat as well. However, for authentic deep-fried food like classic fish and chips, a traditional deep fryer still wins.

faq.question: Are air fryers really healthier?
faq.answer: Yes, air fryers offer significant health benefits backed by scientific research. The 70 to 80% reduction in fat is the main advantage: a 200 g serving of fries contains about 4 g of fat when air-fried, compared with 17 g when deep-fried. Hot-air cooking also reduces acrylamide formation by up to 90% compared with deep frying, according to research published in the Journal of Food Science. Thanks to shorter cooking times, air fryers also preserve more of the vitamins and nutrients in food. Keep in mind, though, that ultra-processed foods remain ultra-processed whatever the cooking method — even air-fried, factory-made nuggets are still processed food. For the best results for your health, use your air fryer with fresh, whole ingredients.

faq.question: How long does an air fryer last?
faq.answer: Based on verified buyer reviews and published tests, a quality air fryer lasts 5 to 8 years on average with regular care. The key factors that affect longevity are the quality of the non-stick coating (ceramic models tend to outlast Teflon ones), the sturdiness of the drawer mechanism and the quality of the heating element. In our comparisons, Philips and Ninja consistently score highest for durability, according to buyer feedback over several years of use. To maximize lifespan, clean it after every use, avoid metal utensils on the non-stick surface and never overload the basket beyond its recommended capacity.

faq.question: What's the best budget air fryer in 2026?
faq.answer: The best budget air fryer in 2026 is the Cosori Lite (3.8 L / 4 qt), which earns an impressive Nura Score of 7.8/10 despite its affordable price. It offers 1,500 W of power, 4 automatic programs and a basket large enough for 2 or 3 people. In second place, the Xiaomi Smart Air Fryer Pro (4 L / 4.2 qt) stands out with Wi-Fi connectivity and control through the Mi Home app — a rare luxury at this price point. The Moulinex Easy Fry Max (5 L / 5.3 qt) offers the largest capacity in the budget segment. Our criteria for budget models (under $150): proven reliability, a durable non-stick coating, easy cleaning and modest energy use. In Europe, all of these models carry at least a 2-year warranty; check the warranty on the listing before you buy.

faq.question: How is the Nura Score calculated?
faq.answer: The Nura Score is our rating system, calculated out of 10 across 5 weighted criteria. We do not test products ourselves: each score draws on manufacturer specification sheets, cross-checked verified buyer reviews (Amazon, Google) and tests published by the specialist press. Cooking quality (30%): crispiness, even browning and versatility, as reported in verified reviews and published tests. Value for money (25%): reported performance against the price in each European market. Ease of use (15%): interface, automatic programs, cleaning, basket ergonomics and display readability. Energy consumption (15%): rated power, preheating time and published consumption data. Design (15%): materials, fit and finish, footprint and durability as reported by buyers. The Nura Score is updated quarterly to reflect long-term user feedback.
